title.narrative: Advancing Capacity, Community systems, and Enabling Supportive Structures for Persons with Disabilities in the BAY State (ACCESS Project)

description.narrative: ltpgtEnvelope 3: Disability Inclusion- Ensure equitable access, dignity, and protection for persons with disabilities in humanitarian response across the BAY states.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtStreet Child Nigeria is proposing a project to enhance the capacity of civil society organizations and duty bearers to deliver and support persons with disabilities effectively by ensuring the inclusion and empowerment of People Living with Disabilities (PLWD) through local, state, and national actions. The project will focus on promoting their protection, equitable access, and participation by strengthening inclusive program design, expanding access and supporting local organizations of persons with disabilities (OPDs) to lead sustainable change and ensure quality service delivery across four local government areas (LGAs): Jere and MMC in Borno State, Fune in Yobe State, and Madagali in Adamawa State, Northeast Nigeria. ltbrgtThe project will address three main objectives below.ltbrgtI. Enhanced capabilities and capacities of relevant stakeholders, including the State, organizations of persons with disabilities (OPDs), civil society organizations, and community-based actors, to promote, adopt, and sustain actions for disability inclusion.ltbrgtII. Strengthening inclusive advocacy for the adoption, domestication, and implementation of the Disability Bill and other provisions through strategic engagement with key stakeholders at the state, local, and community levels.ltbrgtIII. Strengthened the capacity of community-led actions on prevention and response to protection needs of children, women, and men, including persons with disabilities, and connecting them to available service providers through a coordinated approach.ltbrgt In addition, this project will build on the concluded NHF-funded project for the 1st Standard Allocation 2023 - Nigeria, implemented by Street Child and three organizations of persons with disability (OPDs) in Borno, Adamawa, and Yobe states, drawing lessons learnt and adapting to changes in context. The project will ensure effective quality delivery, monitoring, and capacity strengthening for national non-governmental organizations and OPDs. It will advocate for the passage and implementation of disability laws in the BAY States. The initiative particularly emphasizes providing access to preventive and responsive protection services for women, girls, and children with disabilities who are at risk of abuse, discrimination, exploitation, neglect, and violence. This will involve creating a support system tailored to the specific needs of Persons Living with Disabilities.ltbrgtTo strengthen community support networks, the project will focus on eradicating violence, abuse, and harmful traditional practices targeting persons with disabilities. This will include promoting strategic engagement and awareness to eliminate harmful practices, mindsets, and stereotypes for persons with disability while holding duty bearers accountable.ltbrgtAdditionally, the project aims to enhance the capabilities and capacities of relevant stakeholders at both the state and local levels. By fostering knowledge and understanding, the initiative seeks to promote, adopt, and sustain actions and legislation that foster disability inclusion. Through collaborative efforts and a multi-faceted approach, this project aims to create a more inclusive and supportive environment for People Living with Disabilities in the project-targeted LGAs, ultimately contributing to system strengthening, empowerment, protection, and full participation in society while leveraging existing Street Child funded project across MMC, Jere in Borno State and Madagali in Adamawa State funded by Educate a child and UNICEF on multisectoral approached looking at Protection, Education and Livelihood thematics. ltbrgtlt/pgt
